newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP shares slide on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: BHP shares slide on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in resources giant the Broken Hill Pty Co fell as much as 42 cents or two percent in early Monday trade after BHP said fourth quarter trading conditions were difficult.
In releasing the results of a group strategic review, BHP said its performance would remain flat until the results of the review were implemented and new projects contributed to earnings growth.
BHP shares were down 11 cents at A$19.21 by 11.10 a.m. (0110 GMT), having risen in early trade before the announcement to a A$19.42 high.

Brokers and research directors said the initial reaction had been negative, as it appeared BHP was hosing down analysts' increasingly bullish expectations of a 15 percent rise in BHP's annual earnings per share.
BHP is due to release results for the full year to May 31 at end-June.
Were Stockbroking head of research Craig Drummond said the early reaction would remain muted until analysts had returned from a morning briefing by BHP and distributed their reports.
However, Drummond said it appeared the comments relating to the fourth quarter looked as if BHP wanted to dampen analysts expectations.
"Analysts have been upgrading their forecasts before this," he said.

HSBC James Capel head of institutional David Irons said BHP was sold down aggressively initially on the profit warning but had come back in later trade as investors took a more sanguine view of the overall strategic review.
By 11.50 a.m. (0150 GMT), BHP shares were steady with Friday's close at A$19.32, well off its A$19.00 morning low.
Traders said volumes remained subdued, while analysts and fund managers digested the news.
